concepts.name: surface_discontinuity
patterns: The patches consistently display marks or breaks that disrupt the normal appearance and structural integrity of the material surface.

All patches consistently show areas of disrupted surface integrity, characterized by rough edges, uneven texture, and localized discoloration suggesting material degradation or structural imperfections.

The shared visual pattern consists of localized, non-uniform patches or clusters of material that are either missing or covered by a distinct, lighter-colored material, characterized by highly irregular, non-geometric boundaries.
The common pattern is characterized by sharply defined, high-contrast boundaries surrounding irregular areas of apparent material loss or structural discontinuity.
The patches consistently display lines or zones of structural discontinuity, indicative of breaks or separation within the object's surface material.
Localized, irregular areas of discoloration or material absence disrupting the consistent surface texture.
The consistent presence of irregular, high-contrast white or light-colored patches that disrupt the surrounding uniform reddish base material.
The patches consistently display non-uniform surface defects, primarily appearing as darkened, irregular, or linear breaks that interrupt the smooth continuity of the background material.
The patches universally show localized structural discontinuities, including scratches, micro-cracks, and visible signs of surface degradation or contamination.
The common visual pattern is localized surface discontinuity, characterized by irregular, non-linear breaks, chipping, abrasions, or patchy material degradation.
The consistent presence of physical surface breaches, appearing as voids, cracks, or localized material detachment.
The consistent presence of irregular, patchy, and non-uniform areas of surface material disruption or localized discoloration.
The patches consistently show irregular, non-linear breaks in the material's surface continuity, manifesting as voids, cracks, or areas of missing/displaced material.

concepts.name: linear_surface_crack
patterns: The patches consistently display evidence of physical structural failure in the form of linear, dark, and irregular cracks or fissures.
All patches uniformly display dark, linear discontinuities that represent breaks, fissures, or cracks in the material's surface continuity.

All patches exhibit an irregular, network-like pattern of surface disruptions, typically manifesting as fine, dark linear features (fractures or micro-cracks) that interrupt the original smooth surface material.
The patches consistently show narrow, linear disruptions or fissures across the surface material, suggesting structural weakness or material failure.
The common pattern is the presence of deep, linear breaks, fissures, or cracks that suggest structural integrity failure across the material.
The patches consistently display evidence of structural discontinuities, appearing as irregular cracks, fissures, and lines of material separation that disrupt the homogeneity of the surface.
The consistent presence of linear or irregular breaks that disrupt the continuity of the object's surface material.
The patches consistently display surface discontinuities, characterized by cracks, fissures, and localized material splitting.
The visual anomaly across all patches is characterized by linear streaks, scratches, or cracks, indicating surface discontinuities and material degradation.
The patches consistently exhibit an irregular, linear structural discontinuity, appearing as a crack or fissure that breaches the surface continuity of the object.

concepts.name: irregular_surface_staining
patterns: All patches show localized, irregular areas of dark, disrupted coloration or material blemishes contrasting with the surrounding base material.
The visual anomaly is characterized by localized, non-uniform deviations from the base material's color and texture, involving both discoloration/staining and structural surface irregularity.

The consistent visual anomaly is the presence of irregular, highly contrasting white or light-colored patches and streaks that interrupt the uniform color and texture of the darker underlying material.
The patches consistently exhibit localized, non-linear areas of surface irregularity, characterized by boundary disruption, discoloration, and localized material degradation.
The patches consistently exhibit non-uniform surface damage characterized by patches of discoloration, streaks, and minor physical disruptions (pitting/abrasions).
All patches exhibit localized, irregularly shaped areas of darkened discoloration or spotting on the surface, suggesting superficial material alteration or staining.
The patches consistently display irregular, blotchy, or diffuse areas of discoloration contrasting with the base material, suggesting material staining or subsurface seepage.

concepts.name: discoloration_and_mottling
patterns: The shared visual anomaly is characterized by patches of uneven color, tonal shifts, and disrupted texture that appear stained or absorbed into the material surface.
The patches consistently exhibit non-uniform discoloration and superficial material loss, manifesting as streaks, spots, and patchy pigment disruption across the surface.
The common visual pattern is the presence of localized, irregular pigment or color changes, coupled with surface texture disruption, indicating contamination or compromised material integrity.
The common pattern is the presence of amorphous, patchy areas of altered surface color and stain, suggesting localized material degradation or surface contamination.
The patches consistently display localized, irregularly shaped areas of dark discoloration or staining against the lighter background material.

The patches consistently display non-uniform, patchy surface discoloration and irregular material discontinuities, regardless of whether the defect is surface-level staining or deep material compromise.

concepts.name: crack_network
patterns: The patches uniformly display extensive, irregular, and interconnected networks of hairline fractures, fissures, and surface cracks across the material.
The patches consistently display a pattern of fine, interconnected, linear surface discontinuities, suggesting widespread material cracking.

concepts.name: surface_fracturing_network
patterns: The patches consistently exhibit signs of surface discontinuity, characterized by irregular, fine, and interconnected linear breaks or network patterns of material fracturing.

concepts.name: flaking_material_disbondment
patterns: All patches consistently show an irregular, localized discontinuity characterized by a lighter-colored, patchy disruption that appears to be flaking or separating from the darker, intact surface material.

concepts.name: surface_discoloration_flaws
patterns: The patches uniformly display localized areas of altered pigmentation and surface texture, forming irregular, non-uniform patches across the underlying material.

concepts.name: irregular_material_loss
patterns: The shared visual pattern is the presence of irregular, brightly contrasting, light-colored patches that appear to indicate localized material absence or separation from the main surface body.

concepts.name: patchy_surface_delamination
patterns: The common pattern is localized surface disruption characterized by patchy, high-contrast boundaries suggesting material separation or peeling.

concepts.name: surface_flaking_or_cracking
patterns: The patches consistently display surface discontinuities characterized by irregular, detached, or broken areas of material (such as coating or paint) that contrast sharply with the surrounding substrate, indicating a breach in the top layer.

concepts.name: pitting_and_surface_erosion
patterns: The common visual anomaly is the presence of small, localized disruptions to the continuous surface material, appearing as pits, chips, or points of material loss.

concepts.name: linear_fracture_network
patterns: All patches exhibit evidence of linear, irregular discontinuities, appearing as dark or contrasting lines running through the material surface, suggesting separation or internal structural failure.

concepts.name: blotchy_foreign_deposition
patterns: The common pattern is the presence of irregular, high-contrast patches of light or white material deposited onto or adhering to the darker base surface.

concepts.name: void_discontinuity
patterns: The patches consistently display dark, irregularly shaped areas that interrupt or represent a deficit of material from the solid background surface.

concepts.name: irregular_material_chipping
patterns: The shared visual pattern is the presence of localized, irregularly shaped areas that indicate the physical detachment or loss of surface material.
